explanation: Scan the 64-bit word from low bit to high bit, XORing each extracted bit into a one-bit accumulator. Unsigned right shifts eventually reach zero even when the signed Java input is negative.
timeComplexity: O(w) for w significant bit positions, at most 64; unlike clearing set bits, zero positions are also scanned.
spaceComplexity: O(1): retain only the fixed 64-bit remaining word and one parity bit.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/Parity.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: After each shift, result is the XOR of all bits removed so far. XORing the next low bit preserves this invariant; after the remaining word is zero, result is the parity of every original set bit.
walkthrough: For 13 (1101₂), read low bits 1,0,1,1. The accumulator changes 0→1→1→0→1, so return 1.
edgeCases: Zero has no set bits and returns 0.
Negative values retain their two’s-complement sign bit through the ulong cast.
The minimum signed long has exactly one set bit and returns 1.
